prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1397; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The claimant reported a minor collision in a parking lot and stated that a wrist fracture was sustained when they braced against the steering wheel. No attorney is representing the claimant at this time.

Entry 2: Photos taken at the scene show damage that is mostly in line with the impact described by the claimant. The driver is named on the policy, and the claim has been logged for further review.

Entry 3: Police records and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the incident. Photos confirm some of the reported details, though no independent witnesses have come forward to describe the collision.

Entry 4: The claimant added a few small details when asked to walk through events again, but the core account has stayed the same. The reported wrist injury is plausible given the nature of a crash of this kind.

Entry 5: Medical records show treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved. No earlier injury to the same area of the body is known from prior records.

Entry 6: No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing suggests the damage occurred before the coverage start date. The claim is being carried forward with no further action needed at this stage.
